statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-102554: the readObject methods of Guava's CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet and MapMakerInternalMap sized their arrays from an unvalidated count in the serialized stream, so a small crafted Java serialization payload could force a multi-gigabyte allocation. Guava 4.0 through 33.7.1 is affected; 33.7.2 caps that initial size at 256. Sources: the advisory https://github.com/google/guava/security/advisories/GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94, the fix commit on master https://github.com/google/guava/commit/b931fe9d6d5cf00bc55714ad3308d086f71850fe, the same change on the v33.7.2 release tag https://github.com/google/guava/commit/a0d0c36432c4cc7aa4b5063bab9f20d3d18fe9fc, and the release https://github.com/google/guava/releases/tag/v33.7.2. We unpacked every published gradle-8 package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (16 versions, 8.14.4-r0 to 8.14.8-r0; the x86_64 and aarch64 packages of each version are byte-identical, and 8.14.5-r4 is published for x86_64 only) and inspected every jar, nested jars included. The file /usr/share/java/gradle/lib/guava-33.4.6-jre.jar holds Guava 33.4.6-jre in builds 8.14.4-r0 to 8.14.6-r1 and Guava 33.7.2-jre, under the same file name, from 8.14.6-r2; 8.14.8-r0 also ships guava-33.7.2-jre.jar, holding 33.7.2-jre. Every build also ships /usr/share/java/gradle/lib/kotlin-compiler-embeddable-2.0.21.jar, which bundles a relocated copy of Guava under org.jetbrains.kotlin.com.google.common, including CompactHashSet and MapMakerInternalMap. In every build, the bytecode of that copy's CompactHashSet.readObject and MapMakerInternalMap readMapMaker passes the count read from the stream straight to init and initialCapacity without the cap, while the same methods in the packages' Guava 33.7.2 classes carry it. So no published build of this owner is fixed.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-102554 (GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94): the Java deserialization of Guava CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet and MapMakerInternalMap allocates arrays sized from an unvalidated count in the stream, so a small serialized object can exhaust memory. Guava 4.0 to 33.7.1 is affected; 33.7.2 caps the initial size at 256. Sources: the advisory https://github.com/google/guava/security/advisories/GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94, the fix commit on master https://github.com/google/guava/commit/b931fe9d6d5cf00bc55714ad3308d086f71850fe, the same change on the v33.7.2 release tag https://github.com/google/guava/commit/a0d0c36432c4cc7aa4b5063bab9f20d3d18fe9fc, and the release https://github.com/google/guava/releases/tag/v33.7.2. Read every published gradle-9 package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64 (9.4.0-r0 to 9.9.2-r0; the 9.9.2-r0 aarch64 package has the same index checksum as the x86_64 package read), taking each library version from the Maven metadata and manifest inside the jar under /usr/share/java/gradle/lib, not from the file name. The Guava jar is 33.4.6 in 9.4.0-r0 to 9.8.2-r0; from 9.8.2-r1 it holds Guava 33.7.2 (its Maven metadata and bundle version say 33.7.2, though the file keeps the name guava-33.4.6-jre.jar, and 9.9.2-r0 adds an identical copy named guava-33.7.2-jre.jar). Every published build also ships the Kotlin compiler (kotlin-compiler-embeddable, 2.3.0 to 2.4.21 across these builds), which carries its own relocated Guava copy, including org.jetbrains.kotlin.com.google.common.collect.CompactHashSet and MapMakerInternalMap. In the Kotlin 2.3.0, 2.3.20, 2.3.21, 2.4.0, 2.4.10 and 2.4.21 jars read, which cover every Kotlin version these builds ship (from Alpine 3.23, Alpine 3.24 and Debian 13, including the 2.4.21 jars in the current Alpine 9.9.2-r0 and Debian 9.9.1-2), the relocated CompactHashSet.readObject and MapMakerInternalMap readMapMaker methods still size the allocation from the stream without the 256 cap, which the same methods in the shipped Guava 33.7.2 jar do have. So every build still carries the vulnerable code, and the owner stays affected with no fixed version until that copy is fixed.

CVE-2026-102554 (GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94): Guava 4.0 through 33.7.1 eagerly allocates an array sized by the serialized stream when deserializing CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet or MapMakerInternalMap, so a crafted Java serialization stream can exhaust memory. Guava fixed it in 33.7.2 and on its main branch in commit b931fe9, which 33.8.0 includes: https://github.com/google/guava/security/advisories/GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94, https://github.com/google/guava/commit/b931fe9d6d5cf00bc55714ad3308d086f71850fe. Maven bundles Guava as lib/guava-<version>-jre.jar. Checked every maven package published for Alpine 3.24 on x86_64 and aarch64, including the jars nested in it: each carries exactly one copy of Guava, in that jar. 3.9.16-r0 and 3.9.16-r1 carry Guava 33.6.0, 3.10.0-r0 and 3.10.0-r1 carry Guava 33.7.1, and 3.10.1-r0 and 3.10.2-r0 carry Guava 33.8.0, so 3.10.1-r0 is the first fixed build.

Guava fixed it in 33.7.2 and on its main branch in commit b931fe9, which 33.8.0 includes: https://github.com/google/guava/security/advisories/GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94, https://github.com/google/guava/commit/b931fe9d6d5cf00bc55714ad3308d086f71850fe. Maven bundles Guava as lib/guava-<version>-jre.jar. Checked every maven package published for Alpine 3.24 on x86_64 and aarch64, including the jars nested in it: each carries exactly one copy of Guava, in that jar. 3.9.16-r0 and 3.9.16-r1 carry Guava 33.6.0, 3.10.0-r0 and 3.10.0-r1 carry Guava 33.7.1, and 3.10.1-r0 and 3.10.2-r0 carry Guava 33.8.0, so 3.10.1-r0 is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-102554 (GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94): from Guava 4.0 to 33.7.1, Java deserialization of CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet or MapMakerInternalMap sizes its arrays from a count read from the stream, so a small crafted serialized object can force a multi-gigabyte allocation and an OutOfMemoryError. Guava 33.7.2 caps the initial size at 256 (https://github.com/google/guava/security/advisories/GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94, https://github.com/google/guava/commit/b931fe9d6d5cf00bc55714ad3308d086f71850fe, https://github.com/google/guava/releases/tag/v33.7.2). We unpacked all 23 published activemq-artemis packages in the DHI Debian repository, 2.55.0-0 through the current 2.57.0-8, for amd64 and arm64 (2.57.0-0 was published for arm64 only; no debug-symbol packages are published for this source), including every jar inside them. The standalone Guava library is guava-33.6.0-jre.jar in 2.55.0-0 to 2.57.0-4 and guava-33.7.2-jre.jar in 2.57.0-5 to 2.57.0-8, and in every 33.7.2 build that jar's three deserialization paths carry the 256 cap. But every build also ships curator-client-5.9.0.jar (Apache Curator 5.9.0, the current Curator release), which bundles its own relocated copy of Guava under org.apache.curator.shaded.com.google.common, including CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet and MapMakerInternalMap. In every build, the bytecode of that copy's CompactHashMap.readObject, CompactHashSet.readObject and MapMakerInternalMap readMapMaker passes the stream's count straight to init and initialCapacity, without the cap. So every published build, including those with Guava 33.7.2, still contains the vulnerable deserialization code, and a FIXED range at 2.57.0-5 would be wrong. Pending: whether the relocated Curator copy is reachable by attacker-supplied serialized data in Artemis (for example through JMS ObjectMessage deserialization), or a Curator release that bundles a fixed Guava.
